extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Final Order imposing reciprocal discipline based on a state-court suspension and describing required procedures, notices, compliance during suspension, and reinstatement requirements under the agency's disciplinary regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, the OED Director may file a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline' requesting that the USPTO Director impose discipline identical to that imposed by a state disciplinary authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'Notice and Order Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' informed Respondent and directed that, to contest imposition of identical suspension, Respondent must file within forty (40) days a response containing all information believed sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of identical discipline would be unwarranted based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). Failure to file a response permits a determination there is no genuine issue of material fact and supports imposition of identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for discipline: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's suspension was based on violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) as demonstrated by the state disciplinary order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court suspended Respondent for engaging in unauthorized practice of law; making a false or misleading communication about a lawyer or lawyer's services; engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation; and engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice. Those state-determined ethical violations formed the basis for the USPTO reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension penalty (term and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the Office for a period of one year and one day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension applies to practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO; the Final Order specifies the suspension period 'beginning on the date of this Final Order indicated below.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance during suspension — 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: While suspended, the Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order also grants limited recognition to practice before the Office in trademark and other non-patent matters beginning on the date the Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after that date for the sole purpose of facilitating Respondent's compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to facilitate compliance with § 11.58(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may grant limited recognition to a suspended practitioner for a short period to allow compliance with suspension-related obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Final Order: 'Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office in trademark and other non-patent matters beginning on the date this Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after the date this Final Order is signed for the sole purpose of facilitating Respondent's compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and Official Gazette notice — 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and publish a notice of suspension in the Official Gazette, and shall notify appropriate disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts as provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order requires the OED Director to publish this Final Order; to publish the following notice in the Official Gazette (full sample notice language provided in the Order); and to give notice of the public discipline and reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where the Respondent is admitted, to courts where the Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette notice must identify the practitioner, status, suspension term, regulatory citations, and reasons for suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample notice language included: name and residence, that the individual is an attorney licensed by a named state but not a registered practitioner/authorized to practice patent law before the USPTO; statement of suspension term; citation to violated regulations (e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)); and summary of state-court findings (e.g., unauthorized practice, false or misleading communications, dishonesty/fraud/deceit/misrepresentation, conduct prejudicial to administration of justice). The Order also references posting of disciplinary decisions at the OED Reading Room URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedures — 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspended practitioner must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly states: 'Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement,' indicating that reinstatement is governed by the procedural and substantive requirements in that regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority for action
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order is issued pursuant to statutory and regulatory authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59. Those provisions supply the USPTO Director's authority to impose reciprocal discipline and to publish/notify as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and mailing/certification procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order includes a Certificate of Service describing how the Order was mailed to the Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Certificate states the Final Order was mailed first class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Respondent at specified last known addresses (P.O. Box and street address). The Order notes United States Postal Service records indicating delivery of the Notice and Order to Respondent's street address on May 14, 2011.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond to Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file the required response within the 40-day period results in a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact and supports imposition of the identical discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states Respondent did not file a response; 'Accordingly, it is hereby determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact and that the suspension of Respondent ... is appropriate.' This indicates procedural consequence for not contesting the complaint under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).
